trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Cancun
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrive at Cancun International Airport at 11:00 AM on Flight AA. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and take the ADO public bus from the airport to the Hotel Zone (Zona Hotelera) for around $1-2 USD — a great budget-friendly option. Check in to Cancun Beach Resort and get settled.
day_by_day.afternoon: After dropping off your bags, take a short walk or local bus ride to Playa Delfines, one of Cancun's most beautiful free public beaches. Enjoy the turquoise Caribbean water, relax on the sand, and soak in your first afternoon in Cancun. Bring sunscreen and a towel from your luggage.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to the hotel zone and explore the local area on foot. Grab dinner at one of the nearby casual restaurants or food stalls along Boulevard Kukulcan. Rest up after your travel day.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or coffee at the airport before or after landing — look for a OXXO convenience store for affordable options (under $3 USD).
meals.lunch: Pick up tacos or a torta from a street food stand near Playa Delfines or a local taqueria (budget $3-5 USD).
meals.dinner: Try El Fish Fritanga near the Hotel Zone for affordable fresh seafood tacos and ceviche (budget $8-12 USD).

day_by_day.notes: The ADO bus from the airport costs approximately $8-10 USD and is the most budget-friendly way to reach the Hotel Zone. Avoid tourist taxis at the airport which can charge $30-50 USD. Playa Delfines is free to access and has restroom facilities on-site.

day_by_day.morning: Start your first full day with an early morning walk along the beach near your hotel. The Hotel Zone beaches are beautiful in the morning light and far less crowded. Enjoy a light breakfast before heading out to explore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a local R-1 or R-2 bus (about $0.80 USD) down Boulevard Kukulcan to visit Playa Delfines again at a more leisurely pace, or explore a different stretch of the Hotel Zone beach. Bring snorkeling gear if you have it — the waters near the reef areas offer great visibility. Rent gear on-site if needed for around $10-15 USD.
day_by_day.evening: Head into downtown Cancun (El Centro) via public bus for a more authentic local experience. Stroll around Parque de las Palapas, a lively public square with street performers and local vendors. Enjoy the vibrant atmosphere and pick up souvenirs at budget-friendly prices.

meals.breakfast: Visit a local panaderÃ­a (bakery) or grab breakfast at a market stall in the Hotel Zone for pan dulce, fruit, and coffee (budget $3-5 USD).
meals.lunch: Enjoy fresh ceviche or fish tacos at a beachside palapa restaurant near Playa Delfines (budget $6-10 USD).
meals.dinner: Eat like a local at Parque de las Palapas — try Tacos Rigo or any of the surrounding food stalls for authentic Yucatecan tacos and agua fresca (budget $5-8 USD).

day_by_day.notes: The public buses (Route 1 and Route 2) run the full length of Boulevard Kukulcan and cost less than $1 USD per ride — use them throughout your trip to save money. Downtown Cancun (El Centro) is about 20-30 minutes by bus from the Hotel Zone and offers a much more authentic and affordable experience.

day_by_day.morning: Today is your big adventure day! Take an early morning bus or join a budget group tour to Cenote Dos Ojos, one of the most spectacular cenotes in the Yucatan Peninsula. The cenote is located near Tulum, about 1.5-2 hours from Cancun. Book a group tour in advance for the best budget rates (approximately $40-60 USD including transport and entrance).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Cenote Dos Ojos — snorkel through the crystal-clear freshwater cave systems and marvel at the stalactites and stalagmites. The cenote has two main sections: the Bat Cave and the Barbie Line, both offering stunning underwater scenery. Spend 2-3 hours swimming and snorkeling.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Cancun in the late afternoon. Rest at the hotel and freshen up before heading out for a relaxed evening meal. Reflect on the incredible cenote experience.

meals.breakfast: Eat before departing — grab a quick breakfast at your hotel or a nearby OXXO or local café (budget $3-5 USD). Pack snacks for the journey.
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch or purchase food near the cenote — there are small vendors selling sandwiches and snacks nearby (budget $5-8 USD). Alternatively, stop at a local restaurant in Tulum on the way back.
meals.dinner: Treat yourself to a sit-down meal at La Habichuela Downtown in Cancun, known for affordable Yucatecan cuisine, or try Mercado 28 food court for a variety of local dishes (budget $10-15 USD).

day_by_day.notes: Book your Cenote Dos Ojos tour at least 1-2 days in advance through a local tour operator or hostel notice board for the best group rates. Entrance to the cenote is approximately $18-25 USD if going independently. Bring water shoes, a towel, biodegradable sunscreen (required at cenotes), and a dry bag for your belongings. No regular sunscreen is allowed in cenotes to protect the ecosystem.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a leisurely morning at the beach near your hotel. Take a long swim in the Caribbean Sea and relax on the sand. This is a great recovery day after yesterday's excursion. Explore the hotel's beach facilities and enjoy the morning calm.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the public bus to Playa Tortugas or Playa Caracol, two popular and easily accessible public beaches in the Hotel Zone. These beaches are great for people-watching and have a lively atmosphere. You can also try paddleboarding or kayaking — look for local vendors offering rentals at around $10-15 USD per hour.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the famous Punta Cancun area near the Forum by the Sea mall and enjoy the free entertainment and ocean views. Browse the shops and enjoy the lively atmosphere without spending much.

meals.breakfast: Cook simple breakfast items if your hotel has kitchen facilities, or visit a local supermarket like Chedraui or Walmart (nearby in the Hotel Zone) for affordable groceries like yogurt, fruit, and bread (budget $3-5 USD).
meals.lunch: Head to Mercado 28 in downtown Cancun for an authentic and affordable lunch — try poc chuc (grilled pork) or sopa de lima (lime soup) at one of the market restaurants (budget $7-10 USD).
meals.dinner: Grab dinner at a casual beachside restaurant or taqueria near Playa Tortugas — look for the daily specials board for the best value (budget $8-12 USD).

day_by_day.notes: Chedraui and Walmart in the Hotel Zone are great places to stock up on affordable snacks, water, and beach supplies. Buying water in bulk from the supermarket is much cheaper than buying individual bottles from beach vendors. Always carry cash in Mexican pesos for the best prices at local restaurants and markets.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget day trip to the nearby Isla Mujeres — a charming island just 20-30 minutes by ferry from Puerto Juárez. The ferry costs approximately $5-8 USD each way. Explore the colorful streets, visit Playa Norte (consistently ranked one of the best beaches in the world), and enjoy the laid-back island atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at Playa Norte on Isla Mujeres — the shallow, calm turquoise waters are perfect for swimming. Rent a golf cart to explore the island (about $40-50 USD for a few hours split among travel companions) or simply walk the charming main street and browse local craft shops.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Cancun on the evening ferry and enjoy a final sunset from the Hotel Zone beach. Head out for a relaxed evening dinner to celebrate your last full night in Cancun.

meals.breakfast: Have breakfast at your hotel or grab a quick bite near Puerto Juárez before catching the ferry (budget $3-5 USD).
meals.lunch: Eat at one of the affordable local restaurants on Isla Mujeres' main street — try fish tacos or a fresh seafood plate at a family-run spot away from the tourist strip (budget $8-12 USD).
meals.dinner: Celebrate your last evening with dinner at La Parrilla in Cancun's Hotel Zone, a popular spot for grilled meats and Mexican classics at reasonable prices (budget $12-18 USD).

day_by_day.notes: To reach the Isla Mujeres ferry, take the public bus to the Puerto Juárez ferry terminal (not the Gran Puerto terminal, which is more expensive). The UltraMar ferry from Puerto Juárez is the most budget-friendly option. Isla Mujeres is very walkable — you don't need to rent a golf cart to enjoy the island, especially if you're on a tight budget.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy your final morning in Cancun with one last visit to Playa Delfines for a sunrise or early morning swim. Take in the beautiful views of the Caribbean and reflect on your trip. Pack up your belongings at the hotel and check out.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure time, spend a couple of hours shopping for last-minute souvenirs at Mercado 28 in downtown Cancun — prices here are much more affordable than Hotel Zone shops. Pick up handmade crafts, hammocks, vanilla extract, and local snacks to bring home.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Cancun International Airport via the affordable ADO bus (approximately $8-10 USD). Arrive at the airport at least 2-3 hours before your departure flight. Enjoy a final meal at the airport or grab snacks from a convenience store before boarding.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy a final breakfast at a local café or your hotel — try chilaquiles or huevos rancheros, a classic Mexican breakfast (budget $5-8 USD).
meals.lunch: Grab a final authentic lunch at Mercado 28 before heading to the airport — try cochinita pibil (slow-roasted pork) tacos, a Yucatecan specialty (budget $6-10 USD).
meals.dinner: Airport dining or pack snacks purchased from a local supermarket earlier in the day to save money on expensive airport food (budget $5-10 USD).

day_by_day.notes: Check out time at most hotels is 11:00 AM or 12:00 PM — confirm with Cancun Beach Resort in advance. You can often store your luggage at the hotel front desk for a few hours after checkout if your flight is later in the day. Keep some Mexican pesos for the bus to the airport and any last-minute purchases. The ADO bus stop is conveniently located along Boulevard Kukulcan.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Cancun International Airport at 11:00 AM on Flight AA. Clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange airport transfer to Cancun Beach Resort in the Hotel Zone. Check-in, freshen up, and get oriented with the resort amenities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely stroll along the Hotel Zone (Zona Hotelera) boulevard to get your bearings. Head down to the resort beach for a relaxed first dip in the turquoise Caribbean waters. Rent a beach chair and umbrella, soak in the sun, and decompress from travel.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a casual beachfront dinner near the hotel to ease into vacation mode. Explore the nearby shopping and dining strip along Kukulcan Boulevard.

meals.breakfast: Grab a bite at the airport or a quick snack at the resort upon arrival
meals.lunch: La Fisheria or Ty-Coz — casual mid-range spots in the Hotel Zone for fresh seafood tacos and sandwiches (~$12–18 USD per person)
meals.dinner: La Habichuela Downtown or Harry's Cancun Steakhouse for a sit-down welcome dinner (~$25–40 USD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Since the flight arrives at 11:00 AM, keep Day 1 light. Early check-in may not be guaranteed — ask the resort about luggage storage if your room isn't ready. Exchange some currency or use hotel ATM for local pesos. Pick up sunscreen and essentials at a nearby Walmart or Chedraui.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Playa Delfines Beach Day — one of Cancun's most iconic and uncrowded public beaches. Arrive early (around 9:00 AM) to claim a great spot. Enjoy the stunning open-ocean views, the famous 'CANCUN' sign for photos, and the natural beauty away from the resort crowds. No vendors or fees — bring your own snacks and water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue enjoying Playa Delfines or walk the shoreline toward the quieter southern end of the beach. Around 2:00 PM, head back toward the Hotel Zone and explore Mercado 28 or La Isla Shopping Mall for souvenirs and a casual lunch break.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort to freshen up, then enjoy a relaxed evening at a rooftop bar or lagoon-side restaurant along Kukulcan Boulevard.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort or a nearby café such as Roots Cancun for smoothie bowls and eggs (~$8–12 USD)
meals.lunch: Pack a cooler with snacks for the beach, or grab street tacos from a local taqueria near Playa Delfines (~$5–8 USD)
meals.dinner: El Fish Fritanga or Labná Restaurant for authentic Yucatecan cuisine like cochinita pibil and sopa de lima (~$18–28 USD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Playa Delfines is a public beach with no lounger rentals — bring your own towels, chairs if possible, and plenty of water. The beach faces the open Caribbean so waves can be stronger here; swim with caution and check flags. Take a bus (R-1 or R-2) along Kukulcan for a cheap and easy ride (~$0.50 USD).

day_by_day.morning: Full-day Isla Mujeres Catamaran & Snorkeling Tour — depart from the Hotel Zone marina around 9:00 AM. Sail on a catamaran to the beautiful Isla Mujeres, snorkel above colorful coral reefs, and swim in crystal-clear Caribbean waters. Most tours include snorkel gear and a guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Isla Mujeres around midday. Explore the charming downtown with its colorful streets, local artisan shops, and laid-back Caribbean vibe. Rent a golf cart (~$40–50 USD for a few hours) to cruise around the island and visit Punta Sur cliffs and the lighthouse.
day_by_day.evening: Return catamaran ride back to Cancun at sunset (most tours return around 5:00–6:00 PM). Enjoy the golden-hour views on the water. Relax at the resort and have a quiet dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure — fruit, eggs, and coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch is typically included on catamaran tours (sandwiches, fruit, drinks). On Isla Mujeres, try Lancheros Beach Restaurant for fresh grilled fish (~$15–22 USD)
meals.dinner: Sunset dinner at Lorenzillo's or Puerto Madero — upscale but mid-range friendly with fresh lobster and seafood (~$30–45 USD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Isla Mujeres Catamaran & Snorkeling Tour in advance as spots fill up quickly, especially in March (peak season). Most tours depart from Playa Linda or Playa Tortugas piers in the Hotel Zone. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a light rash guard, and a small dry bag for your phone. Open bar is often included on catamarans — pace yourself in the sun.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early (around 7:30 AM) for the Xel-Há All-Inclusive Snorkel Park, located about 75 km south of Cancun near Tulum (approximately 1–1.5 hour drive). Spend the morning snorkeling through the massive natural inlet, mangrove channels, and freshwater-saltwater mixing zones teeming with tropical fish.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Xel-Há's many activities: cliff jumping, tubing down lazy river channels, visiting the lookout tower, and relaxing on hammocks over the water. The all-inclusive package covers food, drinks, and equipment — take full advantage!
day_by_day.evening: Return to Cancun by late afternoon (around 5:00–6:00 PM). Rest at the resort, then enjoy a low-key evening with drinks at the hotel bar or a nearby beach club.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the resort before the early departure
meals.lunch: Fully included in the Xel-Há all-inclusive admission — buffet-style with fresh seafood, grilled meats, salads, and unlimited drinks
meals.dinner: Casual dinner at Taco Factory or Antojitos Mexicanos in the Hotel Zone for affordable, delicious Mexican street food (~$10–15 USD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book Xel-Há tickets online in advance for a discount (walk-in prices are significantly higher). The all-inclusive fee (~$100–130 USD per adult) covers everything inside the park. Arrange transport via ADO bus, shared shuttle, or rental car — renting a car for this day gives flexibility to stop at roadside cenotes or Akumal Bay on the way back. Bring water shoes as rocky terrain is common.

day_by_day.morning: Cenote Dos Ojos Swim & Snorkel — depart by 8:00 AM for the Riviera Maya (approximately 1.5 hours south). Explore the legendary Cenote Dos Ojos, one of the world's most spectacular underwater cave systems. Snorkel through crystal-clear freshwater caverns with halocline effects, stalactites, and eerie blue light filtering through the water.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the cenote, stop at Akumal Beach on the way back to Cancun for a bonus snorkeling session with sea turtles in the wild (free with snorkel gear rental). Return to Cancun by mid-afternoon and unwind at the resort pool or beach.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset Cruise Along the Hotel Zone — board a catamaran or sailboat in the late afternoon (around 5:00–6:00 PM) for a breathtaking sunset cruise along the Hotel Zone lagoon and coastline. Sip cocktails, enjoy live music, and watch the sky turn golden over the Caribbean.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort or grab pastries and coffee from a OXXO convenience store for the road
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at Akumal Bay Beach & Wellness Resort restaurant or a local palapa (~$12–20 USD) for fresh ceviche and fish tacos
meals.dinner: Dinner aboard the sunset cruise (light snacks typically included) or dine afterward at La Parrilla Cancun — a beloved local institution for grilled meats and Mexican classics (~$20–30 USD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Cenote Dos Ojos entry is approximately $18–25 USD per person plus snorkel gear rental. The cenote is near Tulum — combine with Akumal for an efficient day trip. For the Sunset Cruise, book in advance through your hotel concierge or online; cruises typically last 2–2.5 hours. Bring a light layer for the evening breeze on the water. This is a perfect penultimate-day combination of adventure and romance.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — enjoy a slow, relaxed breakfast at the resort. Take one last dip in the Caribbean Sea or resort pool. Pack your bags and soak in the final hours of the Cancun sunshine. Walk along the Hotel Zone beach one last time to collect memories (and maybe a few shells).
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, use the afternoon for last-minute souvenir shopping at La Isla Shopping Mall or Mercado 28. Pick up vanilla extract, local hot sauces, hammocks, and handcrafted jewelry as gifts. Grab a final fresh coconut or agua fresca from a street vendor.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the airport for your departure flight. Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for check-in, security, and immigration at Cancun International Airport.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — treat yourself to a full spread on the last morning
meals.lunch: Final lunch at Señor Frog's or Bubba Gump for a fun, casual farewell meal in the Hotel Zone (~$15–22 USD per person)
meals.dinner: Airport dining or an early dinner before departure at a restaurant near the airport such as Chili's or a local café in the terminal

day_by_day.notes: Cancun International Airport can get very busy during peak season — arrive at least 3 hours early for international flights. Confirm your departure terminal (Terminal 2 for most international flights, Terminal 3 for American Airlines). Use remaining pesos for airport snacks or duty-free shopping. Consider a private transfer back to the airport for stress-free travel (~$20–30 USD) booked through the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.afternoon: Head down to the resort's private beach for your first taste of the Caribbean. Relax on a reserved sun lounger with personalized beach butler service. Take a leisurely swim in the turquoise waters and soak in the atmosphere. Explore the resort's amenities including the infinity pool and spa facilities.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset cocktail at the resort's rooftop or beachfront bar. Dinner at La Habichuela Downtown, one of Cancun's most celebrated fine dining institutions known for Mayan-Caribbean fusion cuisine in an enchanting garden setting.

meals.breakfast: Light continental breakfast or room service upon arrival to refresh after the flight
meals.lunch: Casual beachside dining at the resort's beach club restaurant — try fresh ceviche, grilled fish tacos, and tropical fruit platters
meals.dinner: La Habichuela Downtown — signature cocobichuela (lobster and shrimp in coconut curry sauce), paired with a curated wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Since arrival is at 11:00 AM, no morning activities are scheduled outside the resort. Confirm early check-in with the hotel in advance. Request an ocean-view suite upgrade if available. Keep the first evening relaxed to recover from travel.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day Isla Mujeres Catamaran & Snorkeling Tour departs from the marina. Board a premium catamaran with open bar, snorkeling gear, and a gourmet onboard spread. Sail across the crystal-clear waters to Isla Mujeres, snorkel above vibrant coral reefs, and swim with colorful tropical fish. Enjoy the sun deck and complimentary cocktails on the way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Isla Mujeres and explore the charming downtown area. Stroll the pastel-colored streets, browse artisan boutiques, and visit the stunning Punta Sur cliff viewpoint overlooking the Caribbean Sea. Enjoy a leisurely lunch at a waterfront restaurant before the catamaran returns to Cancun.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a relaxing shower and rest. Dinner at Harry's Prime Steakhouse & Raw Bar in the Hotel Zone — one of Cancun's top upscale dining destinations with premium cuts, fresh seafood towers, and an impressive wine cellar.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the resort's main restaurant before departure — eggs benedict, fresh tropical fruits, artisan pastries, and freshly squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Waterfront lunch at Mango Café on Isla Mujeres — fresh grilled lobster, shrimp pasta, and locally caught fish with Caribbean views
meals.dinner: Harry's Prime Steakhouse & Raw Bar — wagyu beef, oysters on the half shell, and a bottle from their acclaimed wine list

day_by_day.notes: Book the premium catamaran tour in advance through the concierge to secure VIP spots with priority boarding and reserved deck seating. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a light cover-up, and a waterproof camera or GoPro for snorkeling. Tour typically runs 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Playa Delfines Beach Day — one of Cancun's most breathtaking and uncrowded public beaches. Arrive early via private car service to claim a prime spot. Enjoy the wide open shoreline, powerful waves, and iconic Cancun sign photo opportunity. Bring premium beach essentials — a cooler with champagne, gourmet snacks, and luxury beach towels from the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a luxurious spa afternoon. Book a couple's or solo treatment at the resort spa — indulge in a traditional Mayan ritual massage, hydrotherapy circuit, or deep-tissue ocean mineral wrap. Follow with time in the resort's infinity pool with a signature cocktail in hand.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset Cruise Along the Hotel Zone — board an elegant private or small-group sunset cruise along the lagoon and coastline. Sip champagne and premium cocktails as the sky turns gold and pink over the Caribbean. Live music or curated playlist adds to the ambiance. Return to shore for a refined dinner.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast with ocean view — smoked salmon bagels, avocado toast, fresh fruit bowl, and cold brew coffee or mimosas
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic-style spread at Playa Delfines — charcuterie, artisan cheeses, fresh fruit, sparkling water, and chilled rosé arranged by the resort concierge
meals.dinner: Lorenzillo's Cancun — a legendary waterfront restaurant built on stilts over the lagoon, specializing in live Maine lobster, fresh seafood, and Caribbean-inspired dishes

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private transportation to Playa Delfines (approximately 15 minutes from most Hotel Zone properties). The beach has no services, so bring everything you need. Book the sunset cruise through the concierge — private charter options are available for a fully exclusive experience. Sunset around 6:30–7:00 PM in March.

day_by_day.morning: Xel-Há All-Inclusive Snorkel Park — depart early for this world-renowned natural aquifer and eco-park located about 75 km south of Cancun (approximately 1-hour drive). Snorkel through mangrove channels, freshwater rivers, and open sea inlets teeming with tropical fish. The all-inclusive package covers food, beverages, equipment, and activities including cliff jumping and zip-lining over the water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Xel-Há at your own pace. Try the floating river drift, visit the observation tower, or relax in a hammock over the water. Enjoy the premium buffet and open bar included in the park experience. Depart mid-afternoon and return to Cancun via private transfer.
day_by_day.evening: Back at the resort, enjoy a leisurely evening. Visit the resort's rooftop terrace or lounge for pre-dinner cocktails. Dinner at Porfirio's Cancun — a chic, upscale Mexican restaurant in the Hotel Zone known for its vibrant atmosphere, contemporary Mexican cuisine, and celebrity following.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure — protein-rich options including eggs, granola, yogurt parfaits, and fresh-pressed green juice to fuel the active day
meals.lunch: All-inclusive gourmet buffet at Xel-Há — fresh ceviche stations, grilled meats, tropical fruits, and unlimited beverages including cocktails and craft beers
meals.dinner: Porfirio's Cancun — guacamole tableside, duck carnitas tacos, whole roasted fish, and premium mezcal or tequila cocktails

day_by_day.notes: Book Xel-Há tickets and private round-trip transportation well in advance through the concierge. Wear your swimsuit under comfortable clothing and pack reef-safe sunscreen, water shoes, and a dry bag for valuables. The park opens at 8:30 AM — arriving early ensures the best experience before crowds build.

day_by_day.morning: Cenote Dos Ojos Swim & Snorkel — embark on a private guided excursion to the mystical Cenote Dos Ojos, approximately 90 minutes south of Cancun near Tulum. Explore two interconnected underground cave systems with crystal-clear freshwater and dramatic stalactite formations. Snorkel through the ethereal caverns with a certified guide and premium equipment provided.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the cenote experience, stop in Tulum town or the Tulum beach strip for a luxurious lunch. Explore the Tulum Ruins archaeological site perched dramatically above the Caribbean Sea — one of the most scenic Mayan ruins in Mexico. Take a private guided tour for an in-depth historical and cultural experience before returning to Cancun.
day_by_day.evening: Final resort evening — treat yourself to the resort's most exclusive dining experience or book an in-suite private chef dinner on your terrace or balcony with ocean views. Enjoy a nightcap at the resort's bar and reflect on the week's adventures.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast — full hot buffet with made-to-order omelets, fresh pastries, tropical fruits, and premium coffee before the day's journey
meals.lunch: Hartwood Tulum or Gitano Tulum — both celebrated open-air jungle restaurants offering wood-fire cuisine, fresh local ingredients, and craft cocktails in a magical setting
meals.dinner: Private in-suite chef dinner at the resort — curated 4-course menu featuring local Yucatecan ingredients, paired with a premium wine or tequila flight arranged by the concierge

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private round-trip transportation and a certified bilingual guide for the cenote and Tulum ruins excursion through the concierge. The full day trip is approximately 10–11 hours. Bring cash (Mexican pesos) for the Tulum ruins entrance fee. Wear a swimsuit under clothing and bring a change of clothes for the afternoon. Water shoes are recommended for the cenote.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at leisure — enjoy a slow, indulgent breakfast at the resort. Take one last swim in the Caribbean or spend time at the pool. Visit the resort spa for a quick 60-minute farewell treatment — a relaxing massage or express facial to refresh before travel. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time, enjoy a final leisurely lunch at the resort or a nearby Hotel Zone favorite. Take a final stroll along the beach, collect any last-minute souvenirs from the resort boutique or nearby La Isla Shopping Village (luxury brands, local artisan crafts, and gourmet food shops).
day_by_day.evening: Private luxury transfer to Cancun International Airport for departure. Arrive with ample time for premium check-in, lounge access, and a relaxed send-off after an unforgettable week in Cancun.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the resort's signature restaurant — eggs any style, smoked salmon, premium cheeses, fresh tropical juices, and a celebratory mimosa
meals.lunch: La Fisheria in the Hotel Zone — upscale casual seafood dining with fresh catch of the day, shrimp bisque, and craft cocktails with Caribbean views
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or an early dinner at the resort before transfer, depending on flight schedule

day_by_day.notes: Confirm departure transfer with the concierge the evening before. Allow at least 3 hours before international flight departure for Cancun airport check-in and security. Request a late checkout from the resort (typically until 2:00–3:00 PM for premium guests) to maximize your final day. Leave a gratuity for outstanding resort staff.
